newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. urges voters to back $1 bln water bond.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. urges voters to back $1 bln water bond.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson Thursday called on state voters to approve a $1 billion water bond measure, warning that its failure could undermine water supplies and hurt the economy.

"California stands at a critical crossroads," said the Republican governor said. "We can take advantage of the window of opportunity created by Proposition 204 and the federal commitment of matching funds, or we can maintain the status quo which will lead to uncertain water supplies and devastating economic and environmental impacts."
Congress and the White House have approved $430 million in federal matching funds for improvements to the state's water supply infrastructure, Wilson said.

Appropriation of the federal matching funds will be contingent upon the passage of Proposition 204, the Safe, Clean and Reliable Water Supply Act of 1996, which will appear on the ballot on November 5.

Proposition 204 is a $995 million bond measure that would help the state meet federal safe drinking water standards, and provide funds for ecosystem restoration, water conservation and clean water programs.
